title: Synthesis and Use of the Bifunctional Sulfenic Acid Probe BCN-E-BCN for In Vitro and Cell-Based Assays of Protein Oxidation
protocol: Reconstitute cyclooctadiene with CuSO4 and ethyl diazoacetate.
Heat the mixture at 68°C for 2 hours.
Separate the isomers by column chromatography.
Reduce the separated isomers using LiAlH4 from 0°C to room temperature (rt) for 1 hour.
Brominate the reduced compound with Br2 in dichloromethane (DCM) from 0°C to rt for 1 hour.
Treat the brominated compound with potassium tert-butoxide (KOtBu) from 0°C to 66°C for 2 hours.
React the treated compound with p-nitrophenyl chloroformate, pyridine, and DCM at rt for 1 hour.
Mix ethylenediamine, triethylamine (NEt3), and dimethylformamide (DMF) at rt for 2 hours.
Quench excess potassium tert-butoxide with ammonium chloride during extraction.
Perform rotary evaporation of the reaction solvent after quenching.
Afford the strained alkyne as a white solid using column chromatography with ethyl acetate and dichloromethane mixture.
Couple with p-nitrophenyl chloroformate followed by ethylenediamine to afford sulfenic acid probe 1 in good yields.
Charge a flame-dried, 2-neck 250-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar.
Add 1,5-cyclooctadiene (8.0 ml, 65.2 mmol) and hexane (180 ml).
Add anhydrous copper (II) sulfate (2.600 g, 10.2 mmol).
Heat the suspension to reflux (>68°C) with moderate stirring.
While the mixture is at reflux, add a solution of ethyl diazoacetate (7.6 ml, 64.7 mmol) diluted in hexane (17 ml) dropwise over 30 min using a pressure-equalizing addition funnel.
Stir the reaction mixture at reflux for an additional 2 hr.
Filter the hot suspension by gravity filtration.
Concentrate the resulting brown solution using a rotary evaporator.
Purify the material by column chromatography, eluting with 0:1 → 1:4 dichloromethane in hexane.
Dry the copper (II) sulfate beforehand and ensure a light grey solid is used if yield is poor due to moisture in the catalyst.
Store dried and purified compounds under nitrogen or argon, cold (4°C), and protected from light.
Add ethyl diazoacetate at a consistent rate over 30 min.
Ensure the reaction mixture is refluxed prior to addition of ethyl diazoacetate.
Store in the refrigerator.
Use neat hexane/heptane to elute excess COD before switching to 1:4 dichloromethane in heptane.
Charge a 100-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, purified ester substrate 3a (1.040 g, 5.35 mmol), and tetrahydrofuran (5 ml).
Cool the flask in an ice bath and bubble nitrogen through the solution for 10 min.
Add lithium aluminum hydride (1 M, 10.5 ml, 10.5 mmol) dropwise at 0°C with moderate stirring.
Allow the flask to slowly warm to room temperature and then stir for an additional hour.
Place the flask in an ice bath and quench the reaction by adding a few drops of cold water.
Add anhydrous magnesium sulfate to absorb the water.
Filter the suspension.
Concentrate the resulting solution using a rotary evaporator.
Use the crude product 4a, a pale-yellow oil, in the next step without further purification.
Charge a 25-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, alkene substrate 4a (747.0 mg, 4.91 mmol), and dichloromethane (5 ml).
Cool the flask in an ice bath.
Add bromine (0.25 ml, 4.88 mmol) dropwise at 0°C with moderate stirring.
Allow the flask to slowly warm to room temperature and then stir for an additional hour in the dark.
Quench the reaction with 10 weight % sodium thiosulfate solution.
Transfer to a separatory funnel and extract the contents with dichloromethane (3 × 25 ml).
Wash the combined organic layers with saturated sodium chloride solution (25 ml).
Dry over anhydrous magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate on the rotary evaporator.
Recrystallize the off-white solid in hot heptane to afford dibromide 5a as white needles.
Charge a 250-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, dibromide substrate 5a (1.950 g, 6.25 mmol), and tetrahydrofuran (60 ml).
Cool the flask in an ice bath and bubble nitrogen through the solution for 15 min.
Add potassium tert-butoxide (20 wt.%, 11.5 ml, 19.1 mmol) at 0°C with moderate stirring.
Heat the reaction mixture to reflux and stir for 2 hr.
Quench any excess base with a saturated solution of ammonium chloride (50 ml).
Remove the tetrahydrofuran on the rotary evaporator.
Transfer the contents to a separatory funnel.
Add distilled water (50 ml) and extract the contents with dichloromethane (3 × 50 ml).
Wash the combined organic layers with saturated sodium chloride solution (50 ml).
Dry over anhydrous magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate on the rotary evaporator.
Purify the material by column chromatography.
Elute with ethyl acetate in dichloromethane (2:98 → 5:95).
Afford product 6a as a white solid.
Charge a 50-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, 6a (200.0 mg, 1.33 mmol), and dichloromethane (25 ml).
Bubble nitrogen through the solution for 15 min.
Add anhydrous pyridine (0.27 ml, 3.35 mmol) followed by p-nitrophenyl chloroformate (335.0 mg, 1.66 mmol).
Stir at room temperature for 1 hr.
Quench the reaction with a saturated solution of ammonium chloride (25 ml).
Transfer to a separatory funnel and extract the contents with dichloromethane (3 × 25 ml).
Wash the combined organic layers with saturated sodium chloride solution (50 ml).
Dry over magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate on the rotary evaporator.
Purify the material by column chromatography.
Elute with 5:95 ethyl acetate in heptane to afford product 7a as a white solid.
Charge a 25-ml round bottom flask with a magnetic stir bar, BCN electrophile 7a (315.0 mg), and 1:1 acetonitrile/N,N-dimethylformamide (12 ml).
Add triethylamine (0.28 ml) to the mixture.
Add a solution of ethylenediamine in N,N-dimethylformamide (1 M, 0.50 ml) to the mixture.
Stir at room temperature for 1 hour.
Concentrate on the rotary evaporator.
Purify the material by column chromatography.
Elute with 2:3 ethyl acetate in heptane to afford product as a white solid.
Wet-load the material using a minimal amount of dichloromethane (diluting with heptane if necessary).
Ensure only 1 equivalent of ethylenediamine is used relative to the BCN electrophile.
Add 1 M solution of ethylenediamine to the substrate.
Expose purified recombinant wild-type cofilin and cysteine-deficient form of cofilin to differing amounts of hydrogen peroxide in vitro.
Label exposed proteins with BCN-E-BCN oxidation probe.
Use copper-free click reaction with azide-PEG3-biotin to label free end of the BCN-E-BCN probe.
Quench excess unreacted azide-PEG3-biotin and precipitate protein using ice-cold acetone.
Resuspend protein pellet in PAGE loading buffer for analysis through western blotting.
Prepare two sets of protein samples, each containing six microcentrifuge tubes: three for cofilin WT and three for cofilin C139A/C147A.
Add 5 μl of protein stock (concentration of 2 mg/ml) to each tube.

For the set designated with cofilin WT, add 10 μl DI water to one tube, 10 μl of a 0.2 mM H2O2 stock solution to another tube for a final concentration of 0.1 mM H2O2, and 10 μl of a 2 mM H2O2 stock solution to the third tube for a final concentration of 1 mM H2O2.

Repeat the previous step for the tubes containing cofilin C139A/C147A, ensuring that each set has 3 tubes of cofilin WT treated with either DI water or H2O2 and 3 tubes of cofilin C139A/C147A treated with either DI water or H2O2.
Add 5 μl of BCN-E-BCN (final concentration of 25 µM) to one set of samples and 5 μl of dimedone (final concentration of 1 mM) to the other set, incubating at room temperature for 20 min.
Add boiling buffer (1× LDS with 10% 2-mercaptoethanol) to the dimedone-labeled samples.
Heat the dimedone-labeled samples at 95°C for 5 min and proceed with western blotting.
Incubate BCN-E-BCN-labeled samples on a tube rotator at room temperature for 1 hr.
Add three times the sample volume (60 μl) of chilled acetone to each sample.
Vortex each sample for a few seconds and cool to -80°C for 1 hr.
Spin the samples in a 4°C microcentrifuge at 16,000 RCF for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.
Leave the sample tubes uncapped for 5 to 10 min to allow excess acetone to evaporate.
Do not let the sample dry out for too long.
Resuspend each pellet in 50 μl of boiling buffer (1× LDS with 10% 2-mercaptoethanol).
Heat each sample at 95°C for 5 min.
Proceed with western blotting, as described in Basic Protocol 6.
Carefully vortex sample to aid in resuspension, taking care not to overdry remaining samples.
Thaw one 50-µl aliquot of BL21 (DE3) E. coli on ice for 10 min for each plasmid.
Add 1 to 20 ng of pGEX-KG-CFL to one tube of E. coli and 1 to 20 ng of pGEX-KG-CFL C139A/C147A to the other tube of E. coli.
Incubate the tubes on ice for 30 min.
Warm two LB-ampicillin agar plates and a 1-ml aliquot of LB broth (Miller) to 37°C during the waiting period.
Set a hot water bath to warm the tubes to 42°C.
Heat shock the bacteria by placing tubes in the water bath at 42°C for 30 s once the initial incubation is over.
Immediately place the heat-shocked tubes on ice for 2 min.
Add 450 µl of LB broth (Miller) to each tube.
Drop approximately 200 µl of the diluted bacteria mixture onto one LB-amp agar plate per sample.
Gently spread the liquid mixture until evenly dispersed and the agar no longer feels wet and slick.
Place the plates in an incubator at 37°C to grow overnight.
Pick a colony of transformed cells expressing either pGEX-KG-CFL WT or pGEX-KG-CFL C139A/C147A to create liquid starter cultures.
Incubate the starter cultures overnight at 37°C while shaking in an incubator.
Dilute the overnight cultures the following morning at a ratio of 1:10 in LB (Miller) containing 100 µg/ml ampicillin.
Grow the cultures in a shaking incubator set to 37°C until the OD600 reaches 0.6 to 1.0, measured using a spectrophotometer.
Induce protein expression by adding 100 µM IPTG and continuing to incubate the cultures for 3 hr.
Pellet cells by spinning the culture down at 4000 RCF for 20 min at 4°C in 1-L centrifuge bottles.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the resulting pellet in 30 ml of bacterial lysis buffer.
Incubate the lysate in a 50-ml Falcon tube on ice for 30 min.
Sonicate the lysate using an amplitude of 25% for 3 min with a pulse on time of 15 s and a pulse off time of 60 s.
Spin down the lysate at 20,000 RCF at 4°C for 30 min and set aside on ice.
Use approximately 300 µl of glutathione sepharose beads per 30 ml of lysate.
Resuspend beads with 1 ml of wash buffer 1.
Spin down at 500 RCF in a 4°C chilled centrifuge and remove the supernatant to wash away residual storage ethanol.
Repeat wash step using wash buffer 2.
Combine the lysate and the washed beads.
Incubate the mixture overnight at 4°C on a tube rotator.
Pour the bead and lysate mixture into an uncapped separation column, allowing the liquid to flow out.
Wash the column with 10 bed volumes of chilled wash buffer 1.
Then wash with 5 bed volumes of chilled wash buffer 2.
Allow the liquid to reach the top of the column bed and then cap the outflow.
Add 10 U (10 µl) of thrombin per mg of recombinant protein.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C overnight.
Remove the cap and collect the flow through.
Wash the column with 1 bed volume of chilled wash buffer 1.
Resuspend 100 µl of ρ-aminobenzamidine beads in 500 µl TBS.
Spin down at 500 RCF in a 4°C centrifuge and remove the supernatant to wash away residual storage ethanol.
Repeat the wash twice more.
Add the newly washed ρ-aminobenzamidine beads to the thrombin and protein mixture.
Incubate the mixture on a tube rotator at 4°C for 30 min.
Spin down the mixture in a 4°C centrifuge for 2 min.
Collect the supernatant containing cleaved protein cofilin that has been separated from thrombin.
Determine the protein yield by carrying out a Bradford assay.
Seed 3 million HEK 293 cells in DMEM in 7 10-cm tissue culture dishes.
Treat 4 dosage optimization dishes with DMSO vehicle control and BCN-E-BCN at final concentrations of 25 µM, 50 µM, and 100 µM when cells reach ∼70% confluency.
Gently rock each plate after adding BCN-E-BCN for dosage optimization dishes.
Incubate dosage optimization dishes for 15 min in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 concentration.
Add BCN-E-BCN with a final concentration of 100 µM to the treatment time optimization dishes when cells reach ∼70% confluency.
Incubate one treatment time optimization dish for 5 min and another dish for 15 min in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 concentration.
Remove cells from the incubator after their respective incubation times.
Place plates on ice.
Aspirate medium.
Gently wash each plate with 5 ml of ice-cold PBS (pH 7.4) twice.
Remove remaining PBS with a micropipette.
Dispense 1 ml of ice-cold lysis buffer onto each plate and rock.
Scrape the plate thoroughly with a cell scraper.
Transfer the lysis buffer containing scraped cells into a chilled and labeled microcentrifuge tube using a micropipette.
Leave samples to rotate on a tube rotator at 4°C for 20 min.
Spin down samples in a 4°C microcentrifuge at 16,000 RCF for 10 min.
Transfer the lysate into new chilled microcentrifuge tubes without disturbing the pellet.
Perform a BCA assay on obtained lysates and normalize protein amounts to 1 mg/ml.
Add 1 mM of azide-PEG3 to each sample.
Proceed with steps 5 to 13 as described in Basic Protocol 4 for the copper-free click reaction of BCN-E-BCN-labeled residues and azide-PEG3-biotin.
Optimize BCN-E-BCN treatment time and dose for different cell types if encountering low protein lysate yields due to high cell death or loss of viable cells.
Carefully vortex sample to aid in resuspension, taking care not to overdry remaining samples if the pellet has been overdried after acetone removal.
Load 10 µg of each sample and 5 μl of protein molecular weight ladder in a 4 to 12% gradient SDS-PAGE gel.
Run SDS-PAGE at 80 V for 15 minutes.
Increase the voltage to 120 V.
Let the SDS-PAGE run for approximately 1 hour, stopping when the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Set up a wide container containing chilled transfer buffer.
Submerge four pieces of filter paper, one nitrocellulose membrane, the transfer cassette, and sponges in transfer buffer.
Remove the SDS-PAGE from the tank and rinse it well in DI water; then crack open the cassette and trim the wells and bottom strip of the gel.

Create the transfer sandwich using the following order: black side of the cassette, sponge, two pieces of filter paper, SDS-PAGE, nitrocellulose membrane, two pieces of filter paper, sponge, and top of the cassette. Gently roll out any air bubbles after placing filter papers on top of the nitrocellulose membrane.
Place the transfer cassette into the tank and carefully pour in the cold transfer buffer, avoiding pouring directly on top of the cassette.
Add an ice pack and top up with transfer buffer until it reaches the fill line in the tank.
Run the transfer at 100 V for 75 minutes.
Remove the membrane and wash it for 5 minutes in TBST at room temperature on a rocker.
Block the membrane in 3% BSA made in TBST for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 4°C on a rocker.
Make a solution using 3% BSA in TBST containing primary antibodies of interest if applicable.
Incubate the membrane in the antibody solution in a sealed pouch for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 4°C on a rocker.
Remove the primary antibody solution and wash the membrane three times for 5 minutes per wash using TBST.
Mix 3% BSA in TBST containing a 1:20,000 dilution of IRDye 680RD streptavidin.
Incubate the membrane with the mixture at room temperature for 1 hour on a rocker.
Add IRDye® 680RD Goat anti-Rabbit IgG Secondary Antibody to the membrane if using samples from Basic Protocol 4.
Add IRDye® 800CW Goat anti-Mouse IgG Secondary Antibody diluted to 1:20,000 if using samples from Basic Protocol 5.
Remove the streptavidin solution from the membrane.
Wash the membrane four times for 7 minutes each wash.
Protect the membrane from light during the washing period.
Image the membrane on a LI-COR Odyssey CL-x.
Optimize azide-PEG3-biotin treatment dose and incubation time for each experiment type.
Increase streptavidin dilution or shorten incubation time.
